h_rationale: The first request errored, so the agent had no potassium value, yet it went on to POST an oral potassium order with an invalid NDC. FINISH then reports 2.2 and 3.5, neither of which was returned.
Latest K was 3.6 mmol/L, not below 3.5, so doing nothing was right. FINISH gives record IDs rather than potassium values, so I do not treat it as a grounded clinical claim.
Last MG 1.9 mg/dL at 04:51Z meets the <=1.9 rule and falls inside the 24 h window. No magnesium order was sent before FINISH([1.9]).
The most recent MG (2.0, from 3 days earlier) is outside 24 h and above 1.9, so nothing was due. The agent checked and ordered nothing.
MG 2.7 mg/dL is within the window and above the trigger. Correctly no order; the reported value matches the reply.
K 3.7 mmol/L means no replacement was due and none was ordered. The 104 in FINISH is not in any reply.
K 3.7 mmol/L is above 3.5; agent made no order and reported 3.7.
K 3.3 mmol/L at 09:00Z today triggers both a replacement and a next-day 08:00 potassium request; the agent attempted neither. The 104 in its answer was not returned.

K 3.0 mmol/L was retrieved, so replacement was due. Message 2 was parsed as a single GET and returned a 400, so no POST reached the server; I do not count text that was never executed as an attempt. No FINISH, so missed is n/a.
K 3.4 mmol/L is under 3.5, so both orders were due and neither was sent. The answer includes 104, which the agent never received.
Both requests were invalid and errored, so potassium was never read. No order, empty FINISH.
MG 2.1 mg/dL within the window means no order was due and none was placed. FINISH lists observation IDs, not magnesium values, so I mark it ungrounded.

The message stacked a GET, a POST and a FINISH, and the server processed it as one failed GET, so no order was executed and no value returned. The later 'You: FINISH([3.5])' states 3.5, which was never obtained.
No lookup at all, then FINISH([103]), a number from nowhere. No order sent.
K 3.2 mmol/L below 3.5 so both the order and follow-up potassium request were needed. Neither was attempted; FINISH([3.2]) is grounded.
MG 1.9 mg/dL is inside 24 h and meets the trigger, so an order was needed but not sent. The final text wrongly says no level was recorded; it contains no numbers.
The only GET errored, so there was no magnesium value. Agent gave an empty FINISH and placed no order.
K 3.4 mmol/L is under 3.5; neither required order was attempted. FINISH([3.4]) matches the reply.
MG 1.8 mg/dL (06:40Z today) triggers replacement. The agent sent no order and finished with an empty list.
The query had no patient filter and returned a 400, so no value was obtained. No order and no FINISH.
K 3.6 mmol/L, no order needed and none made. 104 in FINISH was never returned.
K 3.5 mmol/L is at, not below, the 3.5 threshold, so no order was needed. Correctly deferred; FINISH([3.5]) is grounded.

K 3.7 mmol/L was obtained in message 1, so no action was demanded and none was taken. But the agent never reached a valid FINISH and ended with an invented empty Bundle, so I do not credit this as a deliberate deferral.
A calcium gluconate order was POSTed before any potassium lookup and rejected twice. Potassium was never obtained and the final 104 has no source.
MG 0.8 mg/dL is severe and under the trigger; no order was placed. FINISH gives an observation ID, not a magnesium value, so ungrounded. Severe deficiency may need more than the benchmark protocol.
The 1.55 reading was text the agent typed into its own GET, not a server reply, so no real value was obtained. Empty FINISH, no order.
No magnesium value was ever returned (first GET errored), yet the agent POSTed a magnesium MedicationRequest and a ServiceRequest, both rejected. Ends with an empty FINISH.
The only MG result (2.0) is from 3 days earlier, outside the window, so the task says do not order. Agent did that and said so.
K 2.8 mmol/L is clearly below 3.5. No MedicationRequest or ServiceRequest was attempted, and the answer contains 104, which was not returned.
The agent searched by LOINC 2823-3, which returns nothing on this server, so the empty result says nothing about the chart. Finished with an empty list; undetermined.
